successors.note: Jeanne d'Albret's marriage to Antoine de Bourbon 'passed Bearn to the House of Bourbon' (Bearn page); 'By Henry IV's accession, Bearn became part of the personal lands of the King of France'. Jeanne and Antoine became joint rulers on 25 May 1555 (Jeanne d'Albret page). Bearn kept its own institutions, so this is a union of lands under the Bourbon rulers, not an annexation by France.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1385. 25 September 1347: Fébus told an envoy of Philip VI that Bearn was a land he 'had from God and from no man in the world'; 'The viscounts gave up this title to present themselves as lords of the sovereign country of Bearn.' Bearn proper is the Pyrenees-Atlantiques cells within 50 km of Pau (20 cells, about 5,060 km2). The gazetteer's own Bearn region is all of Pyrenees-Atlantiques (31 cells, about 7,840 km2) and takes in Labourd, Lower Navarre and Soule, which the page puts west of Bearn, so it is not used (a refined region is requested). The Nebouzan (the 7 Haute-Garonne cells of Cliopatria's polygon, about 1,770 km2) is in from the start: the Nebouzan page says 'In 1258, the viscount of Bearn, Gaston VII, acquired Saint-Gaudens and Nebouzan' and that on Gaston VII's death in 1290 Roger-Bernard III of Foix inherited Bearn, so the Nebouzan went to the Foix-Bearn house. Drawn area about 6,830 km2; the Bearn page gives no area. Fix fx-31 (F179): county-of-bearn is the sub-unit of county-of-foix (data/hierarchy.csv, constituent 1347..1552), so it now draws Bearn proper only. Bigorre and the Nebouzan are carried by county-of-foix (its L2, L5-L7, L10 and K5-K7): the County of Bigorre page (opened 2026-11-01) has Bernard VII of Armagnac sell it in 1407 to John I, Count of Foix, 'From then on it is a subsidiary title of the counts of Foix'; the Nebouzan page (same date) has it pass with Bearn to Roger-Bernard III of Foix in 1290 so that 'Nebouzan became one of the fiefs of the House of Foix-Bearn', and does not describe it as part of Bearn itself. The eastern lands of Cliopatria's County of Bearn polygon (0.27-0.93 E: Hautes-Pyrenees, Haute-Garonne, Ariege, Gers) are not Bearn and are also left to Foix.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends in 1452, but Bearn continued under the kings of Navarre. Catherine of Navarre page: she was 'Countess of Foix, Bigorre, and Ribagorza, and Viscountess of Béarn'; after the Castilian-Aragonese invasion of Upper Navarre in 1512 she and John III of Albret fled to Béarn and based themselves at Pau, Orthez and Tarbes. The Kingdom of Navarre page: Lower Navarre, 'along with the neighbouring Viscounty of Béarn, survived as an independent kingdom which passed by inheritance'. The Nebouzan page has it pass through heiresses to the House of Albret, then the Bourbons (undated), and join the crown in 1607; the Jeanne d'Albret page lists Bearn, Bigorre and Foix among her 1555 lands. The 1450 extent is carried forward: no page opened gives a boundary change between 1453 and 1554, but the Navarre titles show no loss either. Fix fx-31 (F179): county-of-bearn is the sub-unit of county-of-foix (data/hierarchy.csv, constituent 1347..1552), so it now draws Bearn proper only. ledger.note: 25 September 1347: Gaston Fébus declares Bearn sovereign. He told an envoy of Philip VI at Orthez that Bearn was a land he 'had from God and from no man in the world', a declaration of independence in the page's words; he confirmed his allegiance for Foix, and paid homage for lands in Agen, Toulouse and Carcassonne on 26 December 1348 but not for Bearn (Gaston III page). Cliopatria starts the row in 1385; the Bearn viscounty is older (Orthez capital since 1242). Capital Orthez. The Nebouzan (Saint-Gaudens) came to the house in 1258 and passed to Foix with Béarn in 1290 (Nebouzan page), so it is in the state from the start. Fix fx-31 (F179): the Nebouzan union is dropped; the Nebouzan page (opened 2026-11-01): 'Nebouzan became one of the fiefs of the House of Foix-Bearn' in 1290, carried by county-of-foix /ledger/2.

1391: Fébus dies (1 August) and the Estates of Béarn name Matthew of Foix-Castelbon heir on 8 August; Charles VI recognised him as sole heir on 20 December 1391. The lands stay together; the line changes from Fébus to the Foix-Castelbon house.
1464: Gaston IV moves his court from Orthez to Pau, the capital from the mid-15th century (Bearn page).

1479: the lords of Béarn take the crown of Navarre. Navarre page: Eleanor, 'Countess of Foix and Béarn', succeeded John II as queen 'for only 15 days' and left the crown to her grandson Francis Phoebus; Catherine succeeded him in 1483 (Catherine page: 'Viscountess of Béarn'; the page gives Francis no Béarn title). A union of crowns under one ruler, not a merger: Béarn stays one land and one dossier.

12 February 1517: Catherine of Navarre dies at Mont-de-Marsan and her son Henry II, by John III of Albret, succeeds her (Catherine page); the lordship of Béarn passes from the Foix line to the Albret house. The land does not change.

ledger.note: 25 May 1555: Bearn passes to the House of Bourbon. 'On 25 May 1555, Jeanne and her husband, Antoine, became joint rulers after her father's death', her lands including Bearn, Foix and Bigorre; the Bearn page: 'Jeanne d'Albret's marriage to Antoine de Bourbon passed Bearn to the House of Bourbon.' The year is the page's; that this ends a separate Bearn state is the researcher's reading, since Bearn kept its sovereign status under the Bourbon rulers. The Antoine of Navarre page lists him as Count of Foix and Bigorre and Viscount of Bearn (not quoted).

wars.name: Hundred Years' War
wars.outcome: Fébus used the French defeat at Crécy (1346) to distance himself from France, was spared reprisals after Poitiers (1356), was compensated at the Treaty of Brétigny (8 May 1360) for the loss of Bigorre with 200,000 guilders and resisted the Black Prince, who nonetheless crossed Bearn with Fébus's permission in 1367. No Bearn border moved.
wars.note: The Bearn page says the Black Prince 'claimed Bearn as a prince of Aquitaine'; the Gaston III page reads the 1367 crossing as 'a de facto recognition of Bearn's full sovereignty'.

certainty.note: Pyrenean valleys and the plain at their foot, with two exclaves in the east belonging to Bigorre (Bearn page); no treaty or survey line in the pages opened. Bearn proper is a 50 km radius around Pau cut to the Pyrenees-Atlantiques, Bigorre the whole Hautes-Pyrenees, and the Nebouzan and eastern lands a Cliopatria polygon: cell sets, not frontiers. Fix fx-31 (F179): Bearn proper only; Bigorre and the Nebouzan are in county-of-foix.

notes: Cliopatria's 'County of Béarn' (1385-1452, three shapes of about 3,800 km2) is not on Béarn: it lies at 0.27-0.93 E, 42.79-43.38 N, on the eastern Hautes-Pyrénées (7 cells), the south-west Haute-Garonne (7 cells, the Nébouzan and Comminges) and one cell each of Ariège, Gers and Spain, and contains no Béarn cell and not the core of Bigorre. It is read as the eastern lands of the Foix-Béarn lord and kept in every correction from 1379, with Béarn proper and the whole Hautes-Pyrénées (Bigorre, ceded in 1379) added; the Nébouzan is the house's from 1258/1290 (Nébouzan page) and is in from 1347. Béarn proper is drawn as the Pyrénées-Atlantiques cells within 50 km of Pau (20 cells, about 5,060 km2) because the gazetteer's 'Béarn' region is all of Pyrénées-Atlantiques (31 cells) and includes Labourd, Lower Navarre and Soule, which the page puts outside Béarn: a refined 'Béarn' region is requested. Area: the drawn shape is about 6,830 km2 in 1347-1378 and about 12,650 km2 (50 cells) in 1379-1389, 1407-1554 and 7,590 km2 in 1390-1406, against Cliopatria's 3,806 km2 (4,299 km2 by cells), a factor of 3.3 at most; the Béarn page infobox gives no area and no page opened gives one for Béarn, Bigorre or the Nébouzan. Bigorre: ceded on 5 January 1390 for a life annuity (Gaston III page, 'temporary cession'), held by Bernard VII of Armagnac by 1407 and sold that year to John I, Count of Foix (Bigorre page): out of Béarn's hands 1390-1406 and back from 1407. The Bigorre page says the Treaty of Brétigny (1360) 'made it decisively French', while the Gaston III page says Fébus was compensated for 'the loss of Bigorre': the pages disagree on who held Bigorre 1360-1379, so the 1379 counterpart is the communities of Bigorre as before. The span is widened: the Béarn page dates the sovereign country of Béarn to 25 September 1347 and the Jeanne d'Albret page puts the Bourbon union in May 1555, so the dossier runs 1347-1555 with new keyframes, not 1385-1452. 1453-1554 is carried forward from the 1450 shape: the Catherine of Navarre and Kingdom of Navarre pages give the titles (Viscountess of Béarn, Countess of Foix and Bigorre) and the union of crowns from 1479 but no boundary change; the 1479 and 1517 events are renames for the Navarre and Albret succession. Not on the pages opened: the 1391-1452 succession beyond Matthew of Foix-Castelbon (Isabelle, Archambaud de Grailly, John I of Foix as lord of Béarn), the date Bigorre went 'to the crown in an exchange of properties', the dates of the Albret and Bourbon passage of the Nébouzan, Henry IV's union of Béarn with the crown (the Navarre page says Lower Navarre and Béarn were incorporated into France in 1620-1624, outside the span). Béarn was tied to the counts of Foix from the late 13th century, so Cliopatria's County of Foix row (1236-1555) and the Kingdom of Navarre / House of Albret overlap this land: the render order should decide which colour wins. No predecessor is named: the viscounty existed before 1347 as the same land under the Foix house. Needs dossiers: Bigorre and the Nébouzan if the map wants them separately; Marsan, Gabardan and Captieux (western holdings, 'part of the Duchy of Aquitaine', Gaston III page) are not drawn. Capital coordinates are modern town centres, not read from pages; Pau (-0.37 E, 43.30 N) is also the centre of the Béarn radius and is not in the gazetteer's places. Page budget (1-2) exceeded by the repair pass: the Bigorre, Nébouzan, Catherine of Navarre and Kingdom of Navarre pages were opened to answer the reviewer. Fix fx-31 (F179, 2026-11-01): the Bigorre gain (1379), loss (1390) and gain (1407) events and the Hautes-Pyrénées, Nebouzan and Cliopatria-polygon cells are removed from this dossier: county-of-foix carries the same events and cells (L5-L7, L10, K5-K7) and county-of-bearn is its constituent sub-unit (hierarchy.csv), so the cells were booked twice. Bigorre was 'a subsidiary title of the counts of Foix' (County of Bigorre page, 1407) and the Nebouzan 'one of the fiefs of the House of Foix-Bearn' (Nebouzan page, 1290); neither page puts them inside Bearn. The keyframes now all draw the same 20 Bearn-proper cells (the shape ids are kept so every Cliopatria shape still has a verdict).
